title: #Rockies pitcher Kyle Freeland said, “I love you guys,” when asked on-field for a message to the fans after the first complete game of his career — in the shadow of Monday’s MLB trade deadline. “I mean, I've had, obviously, some very serious ups and downs throughout my tenure here with the Rockies. But the fans -- especially the fans who show up every single game, you know those fans have your back, and they want to see you have success, he said. “And to be able to hear them, right when I popped out there for the ninth inning, the excitement from them meant the world, gave me a jolt of energy. It was a really cool, situation. I'll be able to hold onto that one for a really long time.”

title: Luis Garcia was in the middle of a career year and he's been fantastic. Leads NL in slug, 4th in RBI and 8th in HR. But he is a poor defender who doesn't run well and he was almost non-tendered this offseaon. The Nationals were not going to get an elite prospect back for him. They went the route of adding as much MLB ready and high-minors pitching as possible. The team that doesn't have pitching and doesn't have much pitching close to helping in the minors just added pitching depth. That was my goal for any Garcia deal. If Cebert doesn't turn into a big league SP, the return could be 'light' in terms of impact but I think they're going to get legit bullpen help and competition out of this deal for seasons to come. If you would've told me before the season that Paul Toboni would turn Garcia into 4 arms who could end up helping in the majors before the season I would've danced a jig.

Throws mostly sweepers with a 95 MPH FB and a CB. ⚾️ Ben Grable is an elite minor league reliever who is 24 and at AA. Could pitch in majors by year's end. He's striking out 13.7 per 9 and has a legit FB that touches 99 with the kind of IVB teams are chasing. Love this get. ⚾️ Best prospect in deal is Jake Cebert because he's a SP. Placed on IL on July 25th. Having very nice year. 82 IP / 75 H / 96 K. He's got a 77th percentile K rate at AA this year. Likely able to help in MLB rotation next season.

title: The JD signing makes me really happy. I remember the day he got traded. The old pre-season #Texans luncheon, saw lots of friends there. News broke near the end of the lunch. Was an incredibly sad process and outcome from what I knew then and now. Pretty clear he didn't want that trade. No football people wanted that trade. Bygones. Players have no control over who drafts them. Or what strangers say about them. Back then, they had little control over the medical care they received in college. Just trying to get into the league, play ball, take care of their people. The medical care JD received after coming into the league was cutting edge. Like sometimes medical care that sports people get ends up translating more to the general public. It's hard maintaining yourself in a 100% injury sport. That JD is still playing despite the challenges of his career makes me incredibly happy. I root for all Texans. That he gets to work with DeMeco Ryans et al as his coaching staff is delightful. What I would wish for anyone I enjoy and still wants to play. Can't wait to see JD smile, play ball. Lots of ways to love the game. And @mikemeltser wins the award for the !!!! Clowney thing in my huge Texans b-roll. 👇Lots of fun people to talk Texans with, Mike is at the top of the list.

The JD signing makes me really happy. I remember the day he got traded. The old pre-season #Texans luncheon, saw lots of friends there. News broke near the end of the lunch. Was an incredibly sad process and outcome from what I knew then and now.

Pretty clear he didn't want that trade. No football people wanted that trade. Bygones.

Players have no control over who drafts them. Or what strangers say about them. Back then, they had little control over the medical care they received in college. Just trying to get into the league, play ball, take care of their people.

The medical care JD received after coming into the league was cutting edge. Like sometimes medical care that sports people get ends up translating more to the general public. It's hard maintaining yourself in a 100% injury sport.

That JD is still playing despite the challenges of his career makes me incredibly happy. I root for all Texans.

That he gets to work with DeMeco Ryans et al as his coaching staff is delightful. What I would wish for anyone I enjoy and still wants to play. Can't wait to see JD smile, play ball. Lots of ways to love the game.

title: As I cover year 2 of Kellen Moore in New Orleans for Back Together Weekend, I find myself reflecting on this particular day in Cowboys/Kellen lore a decade ago. The date was August 2, 2016. Moore was injured in Oxnard during an 11 on 11 drill at training camp when his teammate rolled onto his leg. Moore suffered a broken right fibula and ankle. He was carted off the field with his leg in an air cast. After that Tony Romo then went down in his 3rd preseason game with a back injury. This paved the way for Dak Prescott to become the franchise quarterback, Romo moved to the broadcast booth and Moore pivoted to coaching. I’ll catch up with Moore about this later on NFL Network.

full_text:
As I cover year 2 of Kellen Moore in New Orleans for Back Together Weekend, I find myself reflecting on this particular day in Cowboys/Kellen lore a decade ago. 

The date was August 2, 2016.

Moore was injured in Oxnard during an 11 on 11 drill at training camp when his teammate rolled onto his leg.

Moore suffered a broken right fibula and ankle. He was carted off the field with his leg in an air cast. 

After that Tony Romo then went down in his 3rd preseason game with a back injury. 

This paved the way for Dak Prescott to become the franchise quarterback, Romo moved to the broadcast booth and Moore pivoted to coaching. 

I’ll catch up with Moore about this later on NFL Network.
